facts.text: The White-winged Triller is one of the smaller members of the cuckooshrike family, found throughout mainland Australia.
facts.quote: The white-winged triller (Lalage tricolor) is one of the smaller members of the cuckooshrike family, Campephagidae. It is found throughout mainland Australia

facts.text: It may also live on islands to the north, including New Guinea and eastern Indonesia.
facts.quote: It is found throughout mainland Australia and possibly on the islands to the north, including New Guinea and eastern Indonesia.

facts.text: The male is black above and white below in breeding plumage, and trills cheerfully through much of the day in the breeding season.
facts.quote: The conspicuous male bird—black above and white below in breeding plumage—trills cheerfully through much of the day during the breeding season

facts.text: During breeding, males frequently rise on fluttering wings in song flight.
facts.quote: frequently rising on fluttering wings in song flight

facts.text: The breeding season runs from mid-spring to early summer, when the bird moves to cooler southern Australia.
facts.quote: the breeding season (mid-spring to early summer)

facts.text: The female is similarly patterned to the male but in dull fawns and white.
facts.quote: The female is similarly patterned but in dull fawns and white.

facts.text: Outside the breeding season, males look like females, keeping blackish feathers only on the wings and tail.
facts.quote: In the non-breeding season, male birds appear similar to the female, retaining blackish feathers only on the wings and tail.

facts.text: It eats a variety of insects, taken on the ground, from foliage, or in the air.
facts.quote: white-winged trillers eat a variety of insects, which are taken on the ground, from foliage, or in the air

facts.text: The Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay people of northern New South Wales call it wiigurrun.gurrun, an onomatopoeic name.
facts.quote: The Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay people of northern New South Wales use the onomatopoeic name wiigurrun.gurrun to refer to this species.

facts.text: It favours woodland and open scrub, and stays close to riverbeds in the central arid zone.
facts.quote: White-winged trillers are fairly common in woodland, and open scrub through most of their range, and close to riverbeds in the central arid zone.
